correctness.rationale: The envelope construction is an exact L-infinity isotonic best fit. The complete-pair seminorm quotient permits binary-cut reduction on each affine permutation chamber. Exact integer enumeration of every 24,308 chamber-cut case at n=2,…,6 gives 1,1,1,1,9/8. An explicit same-chamber 6-site perturbation attains 9/8. The dimension-independent family has exactly two zero inputs and k-versus-(n-k) output levels, producing the asserted lower bound; positive stochastic Jacobians give the general upper bound. All required computation is reproducible with bundled standard-library Python.

originality.rationale: The precise midpoint Chebyshev map is explicitly classical (Stout 2012 Section 2.1); there is no claim to invent it. The inspected work gives formulae and algorithms for the selector, and the 2017 contraction paper treats Euclidean least-squares isotonic projection. None of the inspected material establishes the sharp complete-pair Gini constants 1 through five sites and 9/8 at six, or the explicit linearly diverging lower-bound family. Targeted searches of public literature and research-result records found no equivalently strong statement. This is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of nonexistence or historical priority.

value.rationale: Basic Chebyshev selection is a natural standard representative of nonunique monotone best fits. The exact first-dimensional failure (six sites) distinguishes maximum-norm nonexpansivity from complete-pair dispersion stability, and the explicit all-dimensional family shows the instability diverges linearly rather than remaining a small exceptional defect. The exact finite cutoff and growth order are usable in perturbation/error assessment for shape-preserving smoothing; the result is not merely a numerical table or a reformulation of the selector definition.
